review_title: 3.0 out of 5 stars My experience with this order
review_text: I ordered the phone, but unfortunately received it with a broken screen. I placed a return request immediately. The pickup was scheduled within 3–4 days, but no one came. The app kept showing updates like “unable to contact customer” or “unable to locate address,” which wasn’t true, and then the return was cancelled. I placed the return again, but the same thing happened — no pickup and after 4 days, auto-cancellation. On the third attempt, the pickup person finally came on the last day of the return window, but then refused to take the phone, saying the “quality check failed.” During all these attempts, I had to call customer support many times, as every day passed without action. After the third failed pickup, I was told that returns had already failed multiple times, so an investigation would be needed, and I’d have to wait 5–6 days. After that, i contacted them again. It was only after a fourth return request that the pickup was finally done, after 4 days, the return was completed, and after further 7 days, I got my refund. In total, almost a month was lost in this entire process. About the delivery experience (Delhivery): The same delivery person came twice. He didn’t come to the doorstep, stood at a distance, and spoke in a way that felt quite impolite and mannerless. As this was my first return on Amazon, I was unaware of the process and asked him how it works. Instead of guiding properly, his response felt very unprofessional and rude. I’ve always had good experiences with Amazon’s own delivery staff previously, but this one was disappointing. (Amazon's delivery operations are currently handled by a third-party 'Delhivery' company) Final Review: Though I received a damaged phone, all accessories were present, and the design looked great. Based on the specs, it seemed like a very good phone under ₹10,000. I don’t have any complaints about the product itself. For other customers: If you’re planning to buy electronics or expensive items from Amazon, just be aware — if a return is needed, it may not be as smooth as expected. There may be multiple delays, confusing updates, and even a point where you could be told that the return cannot be processed. Even customer support will not be able to help much. They will only help you reschedule the returns. I don’t think I’ll feel confident buying expensive items from Amazon again unless they are accountable for all aspects of any order, so customer support can truly assist when issues arise. Read more

review_text: i have a lot of phones, as amazon and flipkart already know. but, i do NOT use my mid/high end phones as my daily drivers. my gaming phones are stuck at home and have almost never seen the world outside my house. i will also tell you why i don't use my mid/high end phones outside - because i tend to drop them, crack them, etc. but sometime in august/september i realized that i was doing so many things on my daily use phone that i needed a decent mid range phone. and that is when the search began. i had zeroed in on 4 different mid range phones, but i decided to settle on this one. my main criteria for choosing a new phone was that it had to be decently powerful (able to create a presentation, in the worst of the cases), and MORE IMPORTANTLY, this new phone had to be very light weight. this phone, the iqoo z10r fit the bill in every way, but one (wait for it). the other phone i almost bought, but didn't really, was the tecno pova curve. that's a slim, light weight phone with a decent chipset (7300). it lost in the looks department. but this phone had a lot of things going for it: a solid chipset (7400), great cameras (for a mid range phone, especially with the vivo legacy), fairly slim, and fairly light weight. i have been using this phone as my daily driver for the past few months now, and the iqoo z10r has NOT disappointed in most departments, spare one: this phone is wide! had this phone been a little more wide... this phone would have been a square! holding the phone in a single hand is NOT easy because of how wide the phone is. i am not a fan of the camera bump either. and the light... again, i am not a fan of it. the front camera quality is amazing. rear cameras... i am not so sure. they are okay. my low/mid range infinix, redmi and realme phones probably take equally good, if not better pictures with their rear cameras, when compared to this phone's rear cameras. another big problem: i think this phone could get damaged quite easily given how thin it is. just an hour back i was getting out of my friend's car, and my phone was in between my legs, or maybe i was sitting on it, and the phone fell on a concrete road, as i exited the vehicle. for a minute i thought: there goes my 20k. luckily i had bought a decently tough cover for the phone, so the phone survived (i hope). let's see... we will know if this phone can actually survive a few feet falls onto heavy concrete streets. i have played multiple games on this phone - bgmi, racing games, some low end games, etc, and they all run smoothly. my ancient redmi k50 supports smooth + extreme+, but this phone supports only smooth + extreme. doesn't make much of a difference for me as i am a casual bgmi warrior. overall, this is a good phone for the price, if you can overlook the fact that it is VERY WIDE! review_text: i have a lot of phones, as amazon and flipkart already know. but, i do NOT use my mid/high end phones as my daily drivers. my gaming phones are stuck at home and have almost never seen the world outside my house. i will also tell you why i don't use my mid/high end phones outside - because i tend to drop them, crack them, etc. but sometime in august/september i realized that i was doing so many things on my daily use phone that i needed a decent mid range phone. and that is when the search began. i had zeroed in on 4 different mid range phones, but i decided to settle on this one. my main criteria for choosing a new phone was that it had to be decently powerful (able to create a presentation, in the worst of the cases), and MORE IMPORTANTLY, this new phone had to be very light weight. this phone, the iqoo z10r fit the bill in every way, but one (wait for it). the other phone i almost bought, but didn't really, was the tecno pova curve. that's a slim, light weight phone with a decent chipset (7300). it lost in the looks department. but this phone had a lot of things going for it: a solid chipset (7400), great cameras (for a mid range phone, especially with the vivo legacy), fairly slim, and fairly light weight. i have been using this phone as my daily driver for the past few months now, and the iqoo z10r has NOT disappointed in most departments, spare one: this phone is wide! had this phone been a little more wide... this phone would have been a square! holding the phone in a single hand is NOT easy because of how wide the phone is. i am not a fan of the camera bump either. and the light... again, i am not a fan of it. the front camera quality is amazing. rear cameras... i am not so sure. they are okay. my low/mid range infinix, redmi and realme phones probably take equally good, if not better pictures with their rear cameras, when compared to this phone's rear cameras. another big problem: i think this phone could get damaged quite easily given how thin it is. just an hour back i was getting out of my friend's car, and my phone was in between my legs, or maybe i was sitting on it, and the phone fell on a concrete road, as i exited the vehicle. for a minute i thought: there goes my 20k. luckily i had bought a decently tough cover for the phone, so the phone survived (i hope). let's see... we will know if this phone can actually survive a few feet falls onto heavy concrete streets. i have played multiple games on this phone - bgmi, racing games, some low end games, etc, and they all run smoothly. my ancient redmi k50 supports smooth + extreme+, but this phone supports only smooth + extreme. doesn't make much of a difference for me as i am a casual bgmi warrior. overall, this is a good phone for the price, if you can overlook the fact that it is VERY WIDE! review_title: 5.0 out of 5 stars The Find X9 Series: A Masterclass in Design, Power, and Computational Photography!
review_text: Upgrading to the OPPO Find X9 Series wasn't just getting a new phone; it was an investment in the future of mobile technology. As a long-time supporter of OPPO, I had high expectations, and the X9 has not only met them but completely surpassed them, delivering a truly phenomenal experience that makes every day feel premium. Unparalleled Power Meets Elegant Design From the moment I unboxed it, the design impressed me. The Micro-Arc Ceramic finish feels exquisite in the hand—solid, premium, and distinct. It’s a design that turns heads while feeling durable. Paired with the breathtaking Super-Bright ProX Display, everything is fluid. Scrolling through feeds and watching HDR content on the vibrant, crystal-clear screen feels incredibly immersive. The 120Hz adaptive refresh rate is perfectly optimized by ColorOS, giving the smoothest user experience I've ever had on an Android flagship. The new processor handles heavy multitasking and graphics-intensive games with absolute ease and without overheating—it simply flies. Redefining Mobile Photography The Find X9’s camera system is the true star. I’ve been particularly impressed by the results from the Periscope Telephoto lens. Capturing crisp, detailed photos at 5\times zoom is genuinely transformative, allowing me to take shots previously impossible with a phone. Even more critical is the Low-Light Computational Engine. My evening shots now retain incredible detail and natural color, banishing the overly bright, artificial look you often see. The color science is accurate, vibrant, and always consistent across all lenses. It truly is a photographer's dream. Confidence in the OPPO Ecosystem The seamless integration and refinement of ColorOS demonstrate OPPO's commitment to the user experience. Features are intuitive, customization is deep, and the fast, reliable software updates show that OPPO stands behind its products long after purchase. This attention to quality, from the flagship hardware to the reliable after-sales support, reinforces my faith in the OPPO brand. This device isn't just cutting-edge; it is reliable, showing the best of OPPO's innovation and brand value. Overall Evaluation: The OPPO Find X9 Series is a landmark device. It excels in performance, delivers groundbreaking photography, and is wrapped in a beautiful, premium package. It’s the best all-around flagship phone I have ever owned. 10/10 Highly Recommended!
